description: Use results where the driver started at a grid position numbered higher than 12. Average the per-driver point totals and the per-driver average laps.

a.request: Considering only race results where the starting grid position (`grid`) is higher than 12: for each driver, add up their points and average their laps completed (`laps`), ignoring missing values. Then, across all those drivers, what are the average points total and the average of their average laps, in one row and unrounded?
a.sql: SELECT AVG(total_points) AS avg_total_points, AVG(avg_laps) AS avg_of_avg_laps FROM (SELECT driverId, SUM(points) AS total_points, AVG(CASE WHEN laps GLOB '[0-9]*' THEN CAST(laps AS REAL) END) AS avg_laps FROM results WHERE grid > 12 GROUP BY driverId);

d.request: For results rows with grid > 12, group by driverId, take each driver's SUM(points) and AVG(laps) (skipping NULL laps), then return one unrounded row with the average of the per-driver point totals and the average of the per-driver lap averages.
d.sql: SELECT AVG(total_points) AS avg_total_points, AVG(avg_laps) AS avg_avg_laps FROM (SELECT driverId, SUM(points) AS total_points, AVG(CAST(NULLIF(laps, '') AS REAL)) AS avg_laps FROM results WHERE grid > 12 GROUP BY driverId) AS per_driver;

c.request: For race results where the driver started from a grid position upwards of 12: add up each driver's points and average their laps completed (`laps`), ignoring missing values. Across those drivers, what are the average points total and the average of their average laps? Give one unrounded row. Use results where the driver started at a grid position numbered higher than 12. Average the per-driver point totals and the per-driver average laps.
c.sql: WITH per_driver AS (SELECT driverId, SUM(points) AS total_points, AVG(CASE WHEN laps GLOB '[0-9]*' THEN CAST(laps AS INTEGER) END) AS avg_laps FROM results WHERE grid > 12 GROUP BY driverId) SELECT AVG(total_points) AS avg_total_points, AVG(avg_laps) AS avg_of_avg_laps FROM per_driver;

b.request: For results rows with grid > 12, group by driverId, take each driver's SUM(points) and AVG(laps) with NULL laps ignored, then return the average of those point sums and the average of those lap averages as one unrounded row.
b.sql: SELECT AVG(sum_points) AS avg_points_sum, AVG(avg_laps) AS avg_of_avg_laps FROM (SELECT driverId, SUM(points) AS sum_points, AVG(CAST(laps AS REAL)) AS avg_laps FROM results WHERE grid > 12 GROUP BY driverId);
b.raw: For results rows with grid > 12, group by driverId, take each driver's SUM(points) and AVG(laps) with NULL laps ignored, then return the average of those point sums and the average of those lap averages as one unrounded row.
